title: A crescent Moon over the VLTI
caption: A crescent Moon over an Auxiliary Telescope of the VLTI at sunset, Paranal Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A faint crescent Moon hangs above the round enclosure of one of the four Auxiliary Telescopes at ESO's Paranal Observatory, photographed at sunset by ESO Photo Ambassador Gabriel Brammer.

These four telescopes, together with the four Unit Telescopes of the Very Large Telescope, make up the Very Large Telescope Interferometer, or VLTI. The Unit Telescopes are fixed in place, but each 1.8-meter Auxiliary Telescope can be moved. There are 30 stations on the platform to choose from, allowing a spread of up to 200 meters between them.

That spread is what matters. Interferometry combines the light from several smaller telescopes so that together they act like one much larger instrument, with far sharper resolution. For the VLTI this reaches milliarcsecond resolution, fine enough to make out something two meters across at the distance of the Moon. The round enclosure in the photograph houses one of the telescopes that make this possible.
